title: Khouri Vocab Gap Audit
lede: Everything Dr. Khouri has taught out loud through Thursday 9/3, checked word by word against the 101 notes in your ARAB 101 tree. Both printed vocabulary lists are fully in Anki. What is missing is the second channel she teaches through: the words she builds on the board while teaching letters and correcting dictation, and the phrases she uses in the speaking round. Father and berries both came through that channel.

sections.heading: Not vocabulary, but she expects it
sections.intro: From the Homework 2 page, the two Unit 1–3 quiz pages (vocab quiz and in-class writing quiz, both 9/22), and what she did at the board.
bullets: Write ا ب ت ث و ي in every position and connect them, including the rule that alif and waaw never connect to the letter after them. Homework 2: “practice writing ا ب ت ث و ي for next quiz.”
Her two-step dictation method: first hear which letters are in the word, then pick each letter’s form from whether the previous letter connects leftward.
Hamza on alif at the start of a word: above for a and u, below for i; never on the definite article al-.
The four marks on every taught letter, and the conventions: sukuun is not written at the end of a word, casual text carries no tashkiil at all, and she will not deduct for a missing sukuun.

The speaking round now runs: greeting → ana … / ismii … → maa ismuka? / maa ismuki? → min ayna anta? or min ayy madiina anta? → hal anta min madiinat …? → maa ism abuuka? / abuuki? → ism abii … → tasharrafna → shukran → cafwan → maca as-salaama, with maa … bil-carabi / bil-ingliizi as her vocabulary check.
Unit 3 (pp. 43–55, ج ح خ) is Homework 3, due Thursday 9/11, and the 9/22 vocab quiz says “review all the vocabulary of Units 1–3” — the Unit 3 list is the next thing to card.

method: Sources: the four Teams recordings (8/25, 8/27, 9/1, 9/3) — the Teams captions read end to end, a fresh Whisper large-v3-turbo pass in English and one in Arabic over each full lecture, and an Arabic-script transcription of every silence-bounded utterance (about 4,600 islands) inside every teaching window; whiteboard frames from 9/1 and 9/3; the Alif Baa answer key for drill spellings; Canvas Homework 1–3 and the Unit 1–3 quiz pages; and a dump of every note in the ARAB 101 Anki tree, read from the collection file with Anki closed. Every item in the missing tables was found in the Arabic-script pass at the timestamp given. Heard but not attributable to her, so left off: tamaam and akiid (short, possibly a student or a transcription artifact), and an after-class aside about “baabuuki” on 9/3.
